/-!
# Erdős Problem 469

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/469](https://www.erdosproblems.com/469)
- [Le25] Lewis, Z. J., *On the convergence of the reciprocal sum of primitive pseudoperfect
  numbers*. Preprint (2025).
-/

namespace Erdos469

/-- The proposition that `n` is a sum of distinct proper divisors. -/
def Nat.IsSumDivisors (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ S ⊆ n.properDivisors, ∑ d ∈ S, d = n

open Erdos469

/--
Let $A$ be the set of all $n$ such that $n = d_1 + ⋯ + d_k$ with $d_i$ distinct
proper divisors of $n$, but this is not true for any $m ∣ n$ with $m < n$. Does:
$$
  \sum_{n ∈ A} \frac 1 n
$$
converge?

Yes: the sum converges. This was proved by Lewis [Le25], whose proof has been formalized in
Lean.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/68da20b96673899166e94638f5a7fffeb7231d35/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos469.lean"]
theorem erdos_469 :
    letI A := {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ n.IsSumDivisors ∧ ∀ m < n, m ∣ n → ¬ m.IsSumDivisors}
    answer(True) ↔ Summable fun n : A ↦ 1 / (n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos469

findings.description: The bibliography at lines 24–25 cites Lewis’s preprint as [Le25], dated 2025, under the title “On the convergence of the reciprocal sum of primitive pseudoperfect numbers.” The work linked by the cited Erdős page gives a different preferred title and the year 2026. This is only a bibliographic slip; the mathematical statement and affirmative answer are faithful.
findings.source_evidence: Lewis’s manuscript is titled “Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers” and dated “Version 1.2.1, July 13, 2026.” Its CITATION.cff explicitly gives preferred-citation year 2026. See https://github.com/ZachL111/erdos469-preprint/blob/7cbf74e05504ec6d74a0523c2d6596d59a18e62b/paper/main.tex and the same snapshot’s CITATION.cff.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the author’s preferred title and year: Lewis, Z. J., Convergence of the Reciprocal Sum of Primitive Semiperfect Numbers, version 1.2.1 (2026). Update [Le25] to [Le26] in both the bibliography and theorem docstring, preferably adding a direct source link.

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether the ordinary reciprocal series converges; Lean uses unconditional Summable over the subtype of eligible integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every eligible n is positive, so all reciprocal terms are nonnegative. Extending these terms by zero outside A converts subtype summability to summability of an indicator sequence on ℕ. For nonnegative real sequences, HasSum is equivalent to convergence of the ordinary partial sums. Both equivalences were checked in Lean; Review469.summable_iff_ordered proves the resulting ↔ without using the problem theorem.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization found in either declaration. Scratch proofs establish that the helper agrees with Nat.Pseudoperfect on positive inputs and that A is exactly the set of primitive pseudoperfect numbers. IsSumDivisors 0 is true via the empty sum, but 0 is excluded from A and cannot divide a positive n, so this causes no defect. Computations give A ∩ [0,121) = {6,20,28,88,104}, matching OEIS; 12 is pseudoperfect but not primitive, and 70 is not pseudoperfect. The source’s affirmative PROVED (LEAN) status agrees with answer(True), research solved, and the cited proof endpoint. The external proof contains no explicit placeholders or custom axioms, but its v4.32 source did not rebuild unchanged under the sandbox’s v4.33.1; no independent kernel revalidation of that external proof is claimed. The statement-equivalence proofs in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully and use only standard axioms.
